headline: Nvidia has agreed to pay up to NT$45 billion in advance to Taiwan's King Yuan Electronics for chip-testing capacity at a planned US facility, the company announced.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a confirmed company filing, but the site and timeline are not disclosed.
importance_line: Nvidia paying ahead to secure testing capacity inside the US shows how tight and strategic the last steps of making AI chips have become, which affects chip supply for its customers; the site and schedule are undisclosed, and KYEC's general manager Chang Kao-hsun has previously said a facility takes at least 24 months to build.
summary: Taiwan News reports that King Yuan Electronics (KYEC), a Taiwanese company that tests finished chips, announced on 13 Oct 2026 that Nvidia will prepay up to NT$45 billion (about US$1.4 billion) for testing services at a future US plant run by its subsidiary AeternZ, with the cost deducted from the prepayment once testing starts. The trade outlet digitimes reports that the two are eyeing a Texas site, but Taiwan News says KYEC has not yet disclosed the location or a construction timeline.
notes: digitimes (the pool item) is paywalled; its headline and first sentence agree with Taiwan News on the prepayment. Taiwan News is credited because its text was read.
